nodes.label: Get a California birth certificate
nodes.description: Identify the correct vital records office, choose an authorized or informational copy, and submit the required identity statement.

nodes.label: Choose the copy type
nodes.description: Authorized copies can be used to establish identity; informational copies cannot. Eligibility rules apply to authorized copies.

nodes.label: Choose the correct office
nodes.description: California Department of Public Health and county recorder offices handle copies. The best route can depend on the event date and county.

nodes.label: Submit the application and identity statement
nodes.description: Use the current state or county form and follow notarization and payment instructions for your chosen submission method.

nodes.label: Start and register a business in California
nodes.description: Choose a business structure, register where required, handle tax accounts, and check local permits.

nodes.label: Check licenses and local permits
nodes.description: Use CalGold and your city or county to identify permits and registrations for your location and activity.

nodes.label: Choose a structure and name
nodes.description: Compare legal and tax implications before filing. Check name availability and any naming rules for the structure you choose.

nodes.label: Register the entity if required
nodes.description: Corporations, LLCs, and limited partnerships generally file with the Secretary of State. Other structures may use county filings.

nodes.label: Set up tax accounts
nodes.description: Check whether you need a federal EIN and register for applicable California tax programs.

nodes.label: Get or replace a California driver’s license
nodes.description: Use the California DMV route for a first license, renewal, or replacement and bring the documents listed for that transaction.

nodes.label: Finish online or at a DMV office
nodes.description: Some transactions can be completed online. Others require an appointment, documents, photo, test, or in-person identity verification.

nodes.label: Complete the application and document check
nodes.description: Use the DMV checklist for the exact transaction before visiting an office or paying online.

nodes.label: Choose your transaction
nodes.description: The DMV uses different routes for a first license, renewal, replacement, name change, and REAL ID upgrade.

nodes.label: Get a California REAL ID
nodes.description: Apply through the California DMV, upload or gather the required documents, and complete identity verification in person.

nodes.label: Decide whether you need a REAL ID
nodes.description: A passport or another federally accepted document may meet your federal identification need. Check the official guidance before applying.

nodes.label: Gather the required documents
nodes.description: Use the DMV checklist for proof of identity, Social Security number, and California residency. Requirements depend on your documents and name history.

nodes.label: Complete the DMV visit
nodes.description: Start the application online when available, then bring the required originals to a DMV office for verification.

nodes.label: Apply for California unemployment benefits
nodes.description: Review eligibility, create or use myEDD, file a claim, and keep certifying for benefits while the claim is active.

nodes.label: Certify for benefits
nodes.description: Continue certifying for each period requested and report work or earnings accurately while the claim is active.

nodes.label: File the claim
nodes.description: Use UI Online through myEDD or another method listed by EDD. Save confirmations and respond to follow-up requests.

nodes.label: Review basic eligibility
nodes.description: EDD evaluates work history, earnings, availability for work, and the reason you are no longer working.

nodes.label: Gather employment information
nodes.description: Prepare identity, contact, and recent employer information using EDD's current checklist.

nodes.label: Register to vote in California
nodes.description: Check eligibility, register or update your record, and confirm your status through the Secretary of State.

nodes.label: Check your voter status
nodes.description: Use the state voter status tool or contact your county elections office to confirm your record and election information.

nodes.label: Check eligibility
nodes.description: Review California’s citizenship, residency, age, and status requirements before submitting a registration.

nodes.label: Register or update your record
nodes.description: Use the official online registration system or another state-approved method. Re-register after relevant name, address, or party changes.

nodes.label: Apply for CalFresh food benefits
nodes.description: Submit a CalFresh application, complete the county interview, and provide requested verification.

nodes.label: Submit an application
nodes.description: Apply online through BenefitsCal or use a method offered by your county. You can begin with basic contact information and complete the rest as directed.

nodes.label: Complete the county interview
nodes.description: Your county will contact you for an interview and explain what verification is needed for your household.

nodes.label: Provide requested verification
nodes.description: Submit only the documents your county requests, watch for notices, and use the appeal information on a notice if you disagree with a decision.

nodes.label: Apply for federal disaster assistance
nodes.description: Confirm that your area and loss qualify for an open disaster program, document damage, and apply through DisasterAssistance.gov.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Apply and save the registration number
nodes.description: Apply through DisasterAssistance.gov or another FEMA-approved channel, then respond to inspection or document requests.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Check the declared disaster and available help
nodes.description: Use DisasterAssistance.gov to see whether assistance is available for your location and situation.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Document damage and contact insurance
nodes.description: Photograph damage when safe, keep receipts, and notify your insurer. FEMA may ask about insurance coverage and decisions.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Address immediate safety needs
nodes.description: Follow local emergency instructions first. Government assistance applications do not replace emergency response or insurance notification.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Get an Employer Identification Number
nodes.description: Confirm that your organization needs an EIN, form the entity first when applicable, and apply directly with the IRS.

nodes.label: Apply directly with the IRS
nodes.description: Use an official IRS application method. The IRS does not charge for an EIN.

nodes.label: Form the legal entity first
nodes.description: If you are creating an LLC, corporation, partnership, or exempt organization, complete the state formation step before requesting the EIN.

nodes.label: Confirm that you need an EIN
nodes.description: The IRS explains when a business or organization needs an EIN and when a responsible party may apply.

nodes.label: Apply for federal student aid with the FAFSA form
nodes.description: Create the required StudentAid.gov accounts, gather financial information, submit the FAFSA form, and review school requests.

audience: Contributors to a student’s FAFSA form

nodes.label: Create the required StudentAid.gov accounts
nodes.description: The student and any required contributors need their own accounts. Do not share credentials.

audience: Contributors to a student’s FAFSA form

nodes.label: Review the summary and school follow-up
nodes.description: Correct errors if needed and respond to verification or financial aid requests from each school.

audience: Contributors to a student’s FAFSA form

nodes.label: Gather the requested information
nodes.description: Use the current FAFSA checklist for identity, tax, financial, and school information. Contributor requirements depend on the student’s situation.

audience: Contributors to a student’s FAFSA form

nodes.label: Complete and submit the FAFSA form
nodes.description: Review every section, obtain required contributor consent and signatures, and save the submission confirmation.

audience: Contributors to a student’s FAFSA form

nodes.label: Find government benefits you may qualify for
nodes.description: Use the official Benefit Finder to identify possible programs, then verify eligibility and apply with the agency that runs each program.

nodes.label: Apply with the responsible agency
nodes.description: Use the application link and contact information on the official program page. Keep application confirmations and notices.

nodes.label: Answer the Benefit Finder questions
nodes.description: USA.gov uses your answers to suggest federal and state programs that may fit. You can skip questions you do not want to answer.

nodes.label: Review each suggested program
nodes.description: A suggestion is not an eligibility decision. Open the official program page and check location, income, age, household, or status rules.

nodes.label: File a federal tax return
nodes.description: Determine whether you need to file, gather tax records, choose an IRS-supported filing option, and keep confirmation.

nodes.label: Save proof of filing
nodes.description: Keep the accepted-return confirmation and a copy of the return. Use IRS tools for refund or account follow-up.

nodes.label: Choose a filing method
nodes.description: Use an IRS online filing option, approved software or preparer, or paper forms. Eligibility for free services varies.

nodes.label: Gather tax records
nodes.description: Collect income statements, deduction or credit records, identity information, and prior-year information required by your chosen filing method.

nodes.label: Check whether you need to file
nodes.description: Use the IRS filing requirement guidance for your income, filing status, age, and other circumstances.

nodes.label: Renew or replace a Green Card
nodes.description: Confirm that Form I-90 is the correct route, prepare the required evidence, and file through USCIS.

audience: Conditional permanent residents with limited I-90 situations

nodes.label: Gather evidence for your filing reason
nodes.description: Use the current USCIS instructions for the copy, identity, or biographic evidence that applies to your situation.

audience: Conditional permanent residents with limited I-90 situations

nodes.label: File with USCIS and track the receipt
nodes.description: Use the filing method USCIS allows for your situation. Keep the receipt notice and attend any biometrics appointment requested.

audience: Conditional permanent residents with limited I-90 situations

nodes.label: Confirm that Form I-90 is the right route
nodes.description: USCIS lists the reasons that use Form I-90. Some conditional-resident situations require a different petition.

audience: Conditional permanent residents with limited I-90 situations

nodes.label: Report and recover from identity theft
nodes.description: Create an official recovery plan, secure affected accounts, and keep records as you complete each step.

nodes.label: Contact affected companies
nodes.description: Use the recovery plan to close or secure fraudulent accounts and keep confirmation numbers and correspondence.

nodes.label: Protect your credit files
nodes.description: Follow the official plan for fraud alerts, credit freezes, and reviewing credit reports when those steps fit your situation.

nodes.label: Create an IdentityTheft.gov recovery plan
nodes.description: Report what happened to the Federal Trade Commission and use the personalized checklist it generates.

nodes.label: Keep an incident file
nodes.description: Save the FTC report, dates, names, letters, and proof of each action. A police report may be useful in some situations.

nodes.label: Respond to an IRS notice or letter
nodes.description: Read the notice carefully, compare it with your records, and respond by the method and date printed on that specific notice.

audience: Taxpayers who received an IRS notice

nodes.label: Compare the notice with your records
nodes.description: Check the tax year, amounts, and issue against your filed return and supporting documents before responding.

audience: Taxpayers who received an IRS notice

nodes.label: Identify what the notice asks
nodes.description: Use the notice number and explanation printed on the letter. A notice may request information, explain a change, or require payment or a response.

audience: Taxpayers who received an IRS notice

nodes.label: Follow the notice-specific instructions
nodes.description: Respond using the address, phone number, online tool, and date printed on the notice. Keep copies of everything you send.

audience: Taxpayers who received an IRS notice

nodes.label: Apply for Medi-Cal
nodes.description: Choose an official application channel, submit household information, and respond to county requests or notices.

nodes.label: Respond to county notices
nodes.description: Watch for requests for documents or a decision notice, and use the contact or appeal instructions printed on the notice when needed.

nodes.label: Choose an application route
nodes.description: Apply online, through Covered California, or through your county using the current options listed by the Department of Health Care Services.

nodes.label: Submit household information
nodes.description: Provide the requested information about household members, income, and existing coverage. The exact verification depends on your situation.

nodes.label: Sign up for Medicare
nodes.description: Check whether enrollment is automatic, identify your enrollment period, and use Social Security’s application route when action is required.

nodes.label: Apply through Social Security if needed
nodes.description: Social Security handles Medicare enrollment applications. Medicare.gov explains coverage choices after enrollment.

nodes.label: Check whether enrollment is automatic
nodes.description: Some people receiving Social Security benefits are enrolled automatically; others must sign up.

nodes.label: Identify the enrollment period that applies
nodes.description: The timing and possible consequences of delaying Part B depend on your coverage and circumstances. Use the official enrollment guidance.

nodes.label: Apply for or renew a U.S. passport
nodes.description: Determine whether you must apply in person or may renew, gather the required documents, and submit through an official channel.

nodes.label: Check whether to apply or renew
nodes.description: Your age, prior passport, and its condition determine whether you apply in person or can use a renewal process.

nodes.label: Gather the required evidence
nodes.description: Follow the checklist for your route, including citizenship evidence, acceptable identification, a compliant photo, and the correct form.

nodes.label: Submit through the official channel
nodes.description: Apply in person when required or use the official renewal route. Confirm current fees and processing times immediately before submitting.

nodes.label: Replace a lost or stolen passport
nodes.description: Report the passport so it can be invalidated, then use the correct replacement process for where you are.

nodes.label: Use the route for your location
nodes.description: Inside the U.S., replacement generally uses Form DS-11 in person. Outside the U.S., contact the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.

nodes.label: Report the passport
nodes.description: Report it online, by phone, or by mailing Form DS-64. Once reported, the passport is invalid and cannot be used if found.

nodes.label: Check current processing guidance
nodes.description: Processing options and timing can change. Confirm them on the State Department site before making travel plans.

nodes.label: Report a scam or fraud
nodes.description: Protect yourself first, report the incident to the right official system, and preserve evidence for follow-up.

nodes.label: Preserve evidence
nodes.description: Save messages, receipts, account records, URLs, and report confirmation numbers. Do not upload sensitive information except to the official system that asks for it.

nodes.label: Choose the correct report
nodes.description: Use USA.gov’s router for the scam type. General consumer fraud can be reported to the FTC; internet crime may also belong with the FBI’s IC3.

nodes.label: Stop contact and secure affected accounts
nodes.description: Do not send more money or information. Contact the payment provider or affected company using a trusted number.

nodes.label: Apply for Social Security retirement benefits
nodes.description: Review how timing affects your benefit, gather account and banking information, and apply through Social Security.

nodes.label: Apply through Social Security
nodes.description: Apply online when eligible or use the phone or appointment options Social Security provides. Save the confirmation and respond to document requests.

nodes.label: Gather application information
nodes.description: Prepare identity, work, family, and direct-deposit information using Social Security’s application checklist.

nodes.label: Review when to start benefits
nodes.description: Your claiming age affects the monthly amount. Use Social Security’s estimates and official retirement guidance before choosing a start date.

nodes.label: Replace a Social Security card
nodes.description: Check whether you can request a replacement online; otherwise prepare the documents Social Security requires.

audience: People with a Social Security number

nodes.label: Prepare original identity documents if needed
nodes.description: If you cannot complete the request online, use Social Security's document checklist and application route. Do not mail documents until the official instructions tell you to.

audience: People with a Social Security number

nodes.label: Check online eligibility
nodes.description: Social Security offers an online replacement option for many people. Availability depends on your situation and state-issued identification.

audience: People with a Social Security number

nodes.label: Respond to identity theft separately
nodes.description: A missing card does not always require a fraud report, but suspicious use of your number should be handled through IdentityTheft.gov.

audience: People with a Social Security number

nodes.label: Change your mailing address
nodes.description: Submit an official USPS change of address, then update high-priority government records separately.

audience: People moving within the United States

nodes.label: Update government agencies separately
nodes.description: Mail forwarding does not change your address with IRS, Social Security, immigration, DMV, voter registration, or benefits programs.

audience: People moving within the United States

nodes.label: Keep confirmations and monitor mail
nodes.description: Save each confirmation and check old and new mail channels for time-sensitive notices during the transition.

audience: People moving within the United States

nodes.label: Set up mail forwarding with USPS
nodes.description: Use the official USPS change-of-address site or a Post Office. Avoid look-alike sites that charge unnecessary fees.

audience: People moving within the United States

nodes.label: File a VA disability claim
nodes.description: Check the benefit route, gather service and medical evidence, submit the claim, and track VA requests.

nodes.label: Gather supporting evidence
nodes.description: Evidence commonly includes current medical information and a connection to service. VA lists acceptable evidence and can help obtain some federal records.

nodes.label: Confirm the claim type
nodes.description: VA explains original, increased, secondary, and other disability claim routes. Choose the one that matches what changed or what you are claiming.

nodes.label: Submit the claim
nodes.description: File online or use another VA-approved method. Save the confirmation and copies of uploaded evidence.

nodes.label: Track requests and exams
nodes.description: Check claim status and attend any requested claim exam. Respond by the instructions in each VA notice.
